You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.output: [('arc_periodic_tile_grid_2x2_uniform_window_extraction', 'ARC periodic tile grid: 2x2 uniform-window extraction', 'For this ARC task family, the large input is a periodic background with one data-colored pixel at a fixed position in each repeated tile. Decode the smaller matrix by sampling those positions (respect the tile row/column periods; ignore partial trailing rows/columns or separator-only rows when they are not data). Then scan every overlapping 2x2 window of the decoded matrix: if all four values match, write that color at the window’s top-left coordinate; otherwise write the dominant color of the periodic background. Crop the resulting map to the bounding box of matching 2x2 windows. This reproduces demos: e.g. repeated 2x2 color patches become sparse top-left marks, and larger uniform regions produce overlapping marks. Determine the output background from the dominant base pattern color, not the encoded filler color.'), ('arc_2x2_rotational_mosaic_from_square_grid', 'ARC 2x2 rotational mosaic from square grid', 'For this Continual-ARC pattern, an n×n input grid A becomes a 2n×2n output formed by four rotated copies, not by nearest-neighbor pixel scaling. Partition output into n×n quadrants: top-left=A unchanged; top-right=rotate A 90° clockwise; bottom-left=rotate A 90° counterclockwise (270° clockwise); bottom-right=rotate A 180°. Equivalently, output = [[A, rot90cw(A)], [rot270cw(A), rot180(A)]]. Demos confirm: uniform 3×3 of 4 -> uniform 6×6 of 4; 1×1 [1] -> 2×2 of 1; informative 4×4 demo [[2,2,2,7],[4,2,9,0],[2,8,2,3],[6,5,1,2]] produced the four quadrants in those orientations. Avoid interpreting degenerate uniform demos as simple 2× scaling. On an 8×8 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 16×16 output. A distinctive 10×10 demo with background 6 and sparse colors 3,4,7,8,9 produced exactly these four rotations as quadrants, confirming the rule on a nonuniform case. Validated successfully on task-7acf9041 with a correct first submission. On a 13×13 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 26×26 output.'), ('arc_marker_lattice_uniform_2x2_corners_form_output_cells', 'ARC marker lattice: uniform 2x2 corners form output cells', 'For ARC grids arranged as large uniform-color tiles separated by thin horizontal/vertical separator lines, colored points at separator intersections encode a smaller output. Read the marker matrix at intersection coordinates. Remove outer all-background marker rows/columns (the test may have a blank trailing node column, so output width is based on the active marker bounding box, not the full tiled canvas). For each adjacent 2x2 block of marker nodes, put that marker color in the output cell iff all four corners have the same non-background marker color; otherwise use the tile-interior fill color. Output dimensions are (active marker rows−1) × (active marker columns−1). Evidence: task-53f0c104 demos had 2x2 uniform marker blocks map to that color and other cells map to tile fill; test solved only after trimming the all-background rightmost marker column.'), ('arc_grid_intersections_fill_uniform_2x2_marked_corners', 'ARC grid intersections: fill uniform 2x2 marked corners', 'For ARC inputs with a regular grid of large uniform tiles and colored markers at grid-line intersections, extract the intersection-node matrix P (ignore intermediate tile pixels). The output is one cell per adjacent 2x2 block of nodes: output[r,c] is the marker color iff all four corners P[r,c], P[r,c+1], P[r+1,c], P[r+1,c+1] are the same special marker color; otherwise use the tile-interior fill color. The ordinary grid-line/background color at intersections is not a special marker and does not generate output. Output dimensions are (number of node rows−1) × (number of node columns−1); account for any outer padding or cropped boundary when locating the node lattice. Confirmed by two demos (0 markers on 8 grid background -> 5x5 output with 4 fill; several marker colors on 6 background -> 6x6 output with 1 fill) and a solved test (7/9 markers on 4 background -> 4x3 output with 1 fill).'), ('arc_noisy_filled_rectangles_restore_blocks_and_remove_stray_pixels', 'ARC noisy filled rectangles: restore blocks and remove stray pixels', 'Continual-ARC pattern: a uniform background plus multiple solid axis-aligned rectangular color blocks. Single cells inside a block may be corrupted to other colors or background; unrelated isolated colored pixels also appear outside. Restore each valid rectangle uniformly to its color, and reset outside speckles to background. Infer each exact rectangle from aligned intact rows/columns, not connectivity alone: noise can break connectivity, but a one-cell protrusion outside a block should not expand the rectangle. Preserve all rectangles, even small 2x2 blocks, and verify every edge carefully. On task-7814c09c, demos had backgrounds 9/3/9 and foreground rectangle colors 0/3, 6/8, 7; internal contaminants were corrected, external speckles erased. First test attempt was wrong because of three off-by-one extent errors: a 4 block ended one row too early, a 5 block extended one row too far, and a 2 block was truncated by one row. Correct solution came from checking exact row/column bounds for each rectangle.'), ('arc_object_slides_against_color_2_rail_add_color_8_rail', 'ARC object slides against color-2 rail; add color-8 rail', 'In ARC grid tasks with a uniform full-height vertical color-2 rail and a sparse non-background object on one side, shift the object as a rigid pattern toward the color-2 rail until its bounding box is directly adjacent to that rail. Preserve the object pixels/colors and preserve the color-2 rail. Then add a full-height color-8 vertical rail immediately beyond the far edge of the translated object bounding box (so the object is bracketed between color 2 and color 8). Background cells otherwise stay unchanged. Direction adapts to which side of the color-2 rail the object occupies. Evidence: 22x23 demo had background 5, rail 2 at column 4, irregular 9 pattern shifted left to bbox adjacent to col 4, and color-8 stripe appeared at col 15 just beyond its bbox. Test had background 0, rail 2 at rightmost column 8, a single 6 at row 3 col 7 already adjacent; correct output kept 6 and added full-height 8 rail at col 6. Treat as a pattern hypothesis when the same structure recurs.'), ('arc_boundary_intersection_uniform_corner_cells', 'ARC: recover cells from repeated boundary intersections', 'For ARC grids with a repeating rectangular background cell pattern and special colors placed only at intersections of separator lines, identify the separator row/column coordinates and form the coarse vertex-color matrix. Crop to the region of relevant vertices, then each output cell corresponds to a 2x2 block of neighboring vertices. If all four corner markers have the same color, emit that color; otherwise emit the interior/background fill color of the repeated cells. Output dimensions are one less than the number of vertex rows and columns. Confirmed demos: a 6x7 vertex matrix yielded 5x6 output; a 3x5 active vertex region yielded 2x4. Test task-53f0c104 had rows [0,9,18,27], columns [0,4,8,12,16,20,24], background 3; output matched four-corner unanimity rule. Caveat: crop partial/stray endpoint intersections when demo pattern shows incomplete outer boundary; infer active vertex extent from the regular framed region.'), ('arc_diagonal_color_ray_extension_from_matching_pairs', 'ARC diagonal color-ray extension from matching pairs', "Continual-ARC task pattern: On a uniform-background grid, a compact multicolor cluster may contain same-color diagonal pairs that form ray segments. Direction is away from the rest of the cluster/obstruction. Positive demos: (1) 3,4,1,2 diagonal pairs each extended outward to border; (2) pairs 6,9,5 extended in their clear diagonal direction, while singleton 0 stays unchanged. Negative demos: an unrelated 2x2 with diagonal 7 pair (plus 3,5) unchanged; vertical 4-pair plus 2 unchanged; non-pair pattern unchanged. Solved test: background 8, pair of 2s at (r6,c3),(r7,c4), with further obstruction at (r8,c5)=6, extended 2s backwards up-left to (r5,c2),(r4,c1),(r3,c0). Important: don't extend every diagonal pair blindly; matching pair should belong to a ray/cluster pattern with a clear outward direction. Confirm unobstructed continuation and do not overwrite other colors."), ('arc_shift_non_background_pattern_down_one_row', 'ARC shift non-background pattern down one row', 'In a one-color ARC grid, when the demo shows all cells of the non-background color translated exactly one row downward while background remains fixed, apply a one-row downward translation to that color in the test grid. Keep dimensions; fill vacated top row with background and drop cells shifted beyond the bottom edge. Example demo: 23x2 background 9 with 0s in rows 9–12 moved to rows 10–13. In task-cc5dea9e, background 4 and foreground 8; shifting every 8 down by one row solved the puzzle.'), ('arc_2x2_mosaic_four_rotations', 'ARC: 2x2 mosaic of four rotations', 'For square input grid A of size n×n, output a 2n×2n grid of four rotated copies: top-left = A unchanged; top-right = A rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left = A rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right = A rotated 180°. Preserve all cell colors. Confirmed on task-7acf9041: 6×6 input became 12×12 with exact quadrant arrangement; test 4×4 became the corresponding 8×8 mosaic.
